items.title: 10-year Treasury yields hit 5.04%, a 20-year high and 30-year yields hit 5.4%, a 24-year high. The rise is neither temporary nor close to over. It's the start of a long-overdue reset that'll return interest rates to levels incompatible with current asset prices or debt burdens.

items.title: Sept. consumer sentiment sank to 47.8 from 51.7 in August, while year-ahead inflation expectations jumped from 4% to 4.6%. Warsh may think inflation expectations remain anchored at 2%, but the typical consumers who actually buy the products whose prices are rising so much don't.
items.content:

items.title: Traders now believe if the Fed hikes rates next week, long-term bond yields will fall, as the hike will improve the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility. But the expected hike will be far too little to win the inflation fight, so long-term yields will rise regardless of a hike.

items.title: Markets are now pricing the odds of a rate hike next week at 88%. This should all but ensure a hike. If so, the odds of a second hike in Dec have risen to 74.2%. This knee-jerk rally in markets likely won't last, especially since the rate hikes won't be enough to lower inflation.

items.title: The effective fed funds rate now is 3.63%, just above the 3.4% official inflation rate, but well below the actual rate. Even if the Fed hikes rates 75 basis points by year-end, the effective rate would rise to 4.38%. But if inflation rises faster, that’s effectively a rate cut.

items.title: The August headline CPI came out exactly as expected, up 0.4% on the month and 3.4% YoY. However, the monthly core rose by 0.3%, above the 0.2% expected, but the 2.4% YoY rise matched expectations. If the Fed doesn't hike, it's more proof that 2% inflation is a lie, not a target.

items.title: Treasury yields continue to rise overnight, with the 10-year yield now 4.97% and the 30-year 5.38%. Markets still seem complacent, as most regard 5% on the 10-year as a ceiling. Instead, it will likely be a launching pad, sending yields soaring to levels not seen since the 1990s.
